summary_text: Movilh-Biobío formally denounced (14 October 2016) what it called "brutal and illegal acts of discrimination" at the Hospital Traumatológico de Concepción, where a trans woman was interned in men's beds even though public policy and the legal duty to treat trans people by their chosen name and social sex required the opposite — the complaint was lodged with the Seremi de Salud. (An earlier version of this record cited Law 21.120 as the standard breached; that law took effect in December 2019, after the denunciation.) This remains the closest Chilean analogue to a facility-misassignment incident directly encountered by a visitor: an emergency-room or inpatient visit in Bío-Bío carries a documented risk of gender-mismatched placement. Separately, Concepción's municipality dismissed the staff of its Oficina de la Diversidad y No Discriminación during the January 2025 honourary-staff cuts (~100 workers), which LGBTIQA+ organisations called a "dismantling" leaving one person in post. Bío-Bío held 5.89 % of the national case total in 2024 — third highest — reinforcing that the region's institutional failures occur against an elevated baseline of discrimination reports. Against the national 0.72, this is a −0.10 deviation driven by two concrete traveler-facing findings: the hospital bed placement (medical exposure) and the diversity-office dismantling (loss of local complaint infrastructure). Compared with Valparaíso (0.56), Bío-Bío is 0.06 higher: Valparaíso's problem is the volume of over half the national case load, while Bío-Bío has specific institutional incidents but a normalised share. Compared with Tarapacá (0.64), Bío-Bío is 0.02 lower: Tarapacá's finding is a judicial annulment that devalues trans life in theory, whereas Bío-Bío's hospital episode shows how that devaluation manifests in the care a visitor might actually receive.

sources.title: Denuncian actos ilegales y transfóbicos en el Hospital Traumatológico de Concepción – Movilh Chile
sources.claim_summary: Movilh denunciation (14 October 2016): "illegal and transfóbic acts" at the Hospital Traumatológico de Concepción — although public policies and the legal duty require trans people to be treated by their chosen name and social sex, the facility went "to the extreme of interning a trans woman in men's beds"; the complaint was filed with the Seremi de Salud. Filed by the Movilh-Bío-Bío branch; the episode is institutional (health administration), not criminal.
